ownerDecision.decision: LegalEase may not replace the mandatory SCCA 223A1 GS order form with its custom pleading.
whatWasMeasuredBeforeTheDecision: the string 223A1 appears in no file in the family directory and nowhere in the rendered canonical fixture; the only form the packet names is SCCA 223C, on one route
the rendered componentSet carries no official_form_reference, no records_checklist and no fee_instrument_schedule on any route, while production-field-map.json declares each of them nine times
eleven of the twelve tracks in the SC legal design memo carry destination.kind prosecutor, and the rendered packet is captioned IN THE ......... COURT and asks this court for relief

the memo states for every route that the composed package is not a substitute for the official order form, and that section 17-22-930 makes the solicitor's blank form mandatory and to the exclusion of all other expungement forms
consequences: removed from the first Grade A route cohort
COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN invalidated; the family is WRONG_DELIVERY_TYPE
every affected route removed from custom-pleading commercial eligibility

theSplitTreatmentOrdered.A: Where the mandatory official form is available and participant-filed: use the official form, include every required supporting component, the official-form reference, the records checklist and the fee-instrument schedule, give accurate solicitor-destination instructions, then build and independently verify.
theSplitTreatmentOrdered.B: Where the solicitor supplies, controls or initiates the mandatory form: HANDOFF_READY or GUIDANCE_READY, naming the correct solicitor's office and what the participant must bring or request, stating plainly that LegalEase does not replace the solicitor's mandatory form, with packet checkout disabled.
theSplitTreatmentOrdered.C: Only routes genuinely filed as court petitions may use a court-captioned pleading seeking relief from the court.

whatMayNotBeDone: preserving the current custom pleading because it already has fixtures and visual bundles
a cosmetic repair on a wrong delivery type
ownerDecision.visualReviewInstruction: Neither South Carolina bundle is to be reviewed. Both were published before this decision and are superseded by it.

classificationBasis: Existing owner branch B expressly orders HANDOFF_READY or GUIDANCE_READY where solicitor supplies/controls/initiates mandatory form. existingOfficialOrderManualItems: Obtain SLED criminal history record. Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is the record the solicitor's office and SLED work from, and it is the only reliable way to see every charge and disposition on your record before you choose which one to spend an application on.
Signature on the official order form — The blank SCCA order form obtained from the solicitor's office.
Eligibility recital and statutory-lane election on the official form — Findings block of the SCCA order form.
Alcohol Education Program Director's attestation signature — Attestation block of the official order form.

The applicant signs the application. Under § 17-22-940(E)(3) the applicant may not take possession of the application during the expungement process, so the signature is given at the solicitor's office rather than on a document the participant keeps.

$250 solicitor administrative fee per individual order under § 17-22-940(A), nonrefundable even if the charge is later found ineligible; NO SLED verification fee, because § 17-22-940(E)(1) exempts this route; and the $35 clerk of court filing fee under § 17-22-940(F). The § 17-22-550 programme enrolment fee of $250, and any provider fees, are programme costs; participation may not be denied for inability to pay and those fees may be waived or reduced at the solicitor's discretion.

The solicitor may waive the $250 fee only where a person has been falsely accused as a result of identity theft, § 17-22-940(J). Each solicitor's office also maintains a private donation account which may defray up to fifty per cent of the administrative fee on a first-come first-served basis, § 17-22-940(A)(2).

Signature on the official order form — The blank SCCA order form obtained from the solicitor's office.
Eligibility recital and statutory-lane election on the official form — Findings block of the SCCA order form.

The applicant signs the application. Under § 17-22-940(E)(3) the applicant may not take possession of the application during the expungement process, so the signature is given at the solicitor's office rather than on a document the participant keeps.

$250 solicitor administrative fee per individual order under § 17-22-940(A), nonrefundable even if the charge is later found ineligible; $25 SLED verification fee under § 17-22-940(E)(1); and the $35 clerk of court filing fee under § 17-22-940(F) and § 8-21-310(C)(4), which the solicitor forwards and which is refunded if the charge is found statutorily ineligible. Under § 17-22-940(E), on this route a conviction for any minor traffic-related offence that is not related in any way to driving under the influence of alcohol or other drugs is not considered a bar to expungement.

The solicitor may waive the $250 fee only where a person has been falsely accused as a result of identity theft, § 17-22-940(J). Each solicitor's office also maintains a private donation account which may defray up to fifty per cent of the administrative fee on a first-come first-served basis, § 17-22-940(A)(2).

existingDestination.name: Solicitor's Office in the judicial circuit where the offence was committed
existingDestination.detail: The applicant applies to the solicitor's office. SLED verifies and documents statutory eligibility before the solicitor or his designee and then a circuit court judge sign, and the $25 SLED verification fee applies. Both SLED and the Department of Motor Vehicles retain a nonpublic record after the order.

existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.name: SLED criminal history record
existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.obtainedFrom: South Carolina Law Enforcement Division
existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.howToObtain: Request your own criminal history record from SLED. It is the record the solicitor's office and SLED work from, and it is the only reliable way to see every charge and disposition on your record before you choose which one to spend an application on.

existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.name: Court docket and certified disposition
existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the magistrate, municipal or General Sessions court that handled the case
existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk of the court that handled the case for the docket and, where available, a certified disposition. The docket carries the warrant or indictment number, the court level and the disposition date the application needs.

existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.name: Sentencing sheet and proof that every term and condition was completed
existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court that sentenced the participant, and the supervising probation office where applicable
existingParticipantRecordsRequirements.howToObtain: Ask the clerk for the sentencing sheet, which shows the subsection you were convicted under and whether it was a felony, and for proof that fines, restitution and any other condition are satisfied. The three-year clock runs from the date the last of those was completed.
